components.label: Search controls
components.responsibility: Own typed filter input and explicit loading/error/empty state.

components.label: Search service
components.responsibility: Search an authorized corpus with a declared stable ordering.

components.label: Search API
components.responsibility: Validate typed filters, scope authorization and cursor identity.

components.label: Server search index
components.responsibility: Execute bounded indexed searches and expose dataset revisions.

components.label: Input scheduler
components.responsibility: Issue a new query only after the debounce policy; flush explicit submission.

components.label: Request cancellation
components.responsibility: Abort obsolete network work without assuming every server stops.

components.label: Response revision guard
components.responsibility: Reject responses whose generation or filter hash is stale.

components.label: Bounded result cache
components.responsibility: Key by authorization scope, filter, sort and dataset policy; use TTL and LRU bounds.

components.label: Saved-filter store
components.responsibility: Own account filter versions using authenticated conditional updates.

components.label: Page identity merger
components.responsibility: Merge by stable record ID only within the same query generation and ordering.

components.label: Local prefix index
components.responsibility: Search a bounded authorized downloaded corpus using a trie.

components.label: Index loader
components.responsibility: Fetch a bounded versioned corpus, replace indexes atomically and erase it on scope changes.

components.label: URL/local draft state
components.responsibility: Serialize validated versioned filters; migrate or reject unknown formats.
stateOwnership: draft only; no secrets in URLs

components.label: Unified query coordinator
components.responsibility: Own request generation, cancellation, response application and page merge ordering.

requirements.text: Only responses for the current query generation and filter identity may update the visible results.
Saved filters restore consistently across reloads; account saves use authorization and optimistic version checks.
Page tokens bind ordering, filter identity and dataset policy; merging cannot duplicate result identities.
Debounce, cancellation and bounded caches reduce work without being relied upon for correctness.

problem.scope: Extend autocomplete explicitly with versioned saved filters. A client-side prefix index is limited to an authorized bounded corpus; it is not a general distributed search engine.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Cancellation is an optimization; a response-generation guard is still necessary.
references.title: AbortController

acceptanceCases.given: Request A is generation 1; B is generation 2.
acceptanceCases.when: B returns, then A returns despite cancellation.

acceptanceCases.given: Page two of filter A is in flight.
acceptanceCases.then: The page is discarded; no A record enters B results.
acceptanceCases.when: Change to filter B, then receive page two of A.

acceptanceCases.then: One succeeds at version 4; the other gets a conflict.

acceptanceCases.given: User A has cached results and a local index.
acceptanceCases.then: A data is erased before B queries or renders results.
acceptanceCases.when: Sign out and sign in as B.

guarantees: An abort is not the stale-response correctness mechanism.
Concurrent device edits cannot silently overwrite a newer saved definition.

assumptions: Result IDs are stable within the declared dataset policy.
Saved filters contain an allowlisted AST, not executable SQL or credentials.
solutions.chooseWhen: The corpus is large, private, or requires server-side filtering and ranking.

stages.explanation: Begin with one request path and stable result identities. A response identifies its query generation. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: Request A is generation 1; B is generation 2. B returns, then A returns despite cancellation.
invariants: A response identifies its query generation.

stages.reason: Begin with one request path and stable result identities.
stages.title: Define typed filters and a request path

The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: Page two of filter A is in flight.
invariants: Unauthorized filters never reach a broader corpus.

stages.reason: Expose API validation and the actual index without adding a second authoritative UI state.

The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: Request A is generation 1; B is generation 2. B returns, then A returns despite cancellation.
invariants: A cancelled query can still finish remotely.
Local index replacement is atomic, never half-built.

stages.reason: Keep work-reduction mechanisms separate from correctness.
stages.title: Debounce and cancel obsolete requests

stages.explanation: Response application checks both generation and filter identity. Generation A cannot overwrite generation B. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: Request A is generation 1; B is generation 2. B returns, then A returns despite cancellation.
invariants: Generation A cannot overwrite generation B.
stages.question: What if the oldest request returns last?
stages.reason: Response application checks both generation and filter identity.
stages.title: Guard responses by generation

stages.explanation: Separate shareable draft state from authenticated account saves. Updating a stale saved-filter version returns a conflict instead of losing another device edit. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: Two devices loaded saved-filter version 3. Both update with expectedVersion=3.
invariants: Updating a stale saved-filter version returns a conflict instead of losing another device edit.
stages.question: What exactly survives a reload or another device?
stages.reason: Separate shareable draft state from authenticated account saves.
stages.title: Persist versioned search definitions

stages.explanation: Cache identity includes authorization and dataset scope. Sign-out and authorization-scope changes invalidate cache and local index copies. [A cache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_replacement_policies) keeps reusable results in limited memory. Eviction controls space, while ownership and invalidation rules determine whether a returned value is still safe to use. Consider this case: User A has cached results and a local index. Sign out and sign in as B.
invariants: Sign-out and authorization-scope changes invalidate cache and local index copies.
stages.question: Can another user inherit a cached private result?
stages.reason: Cache identity includes authorization and dataset scope.
stages.title: Add bounded reuse and scope invalidation

stages.explanation: A page belongs to exactly one filter, ordering and query generation. Cross-query pages are discarded and duplicate record IDs appear once. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters. Consider this case: Page two of filter A is in flight.
invariants: Cross-query pages are discarded and duplicate record IDs appear once.
stages.question: What happens when filters change during a next-page request?
stages.reason: A page belongs to exactly one filter, ordering and query generation.
stages.title: Merge pages within one query identity

stages.explanation: A single coordinator owns generation, cancellation and visible page identity. Cache hits and network responses pass through the same generation guard. [A race condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_condition) makes an outcome depend on which operation finishes first. Responses need an identity or generation check so an older request cannot overwrite newer user intent. Consider this case: Request A is generation 1; B is generation 2.
invariants: Cache hits and network responses pass through the same generation guard.

operations.reason: Unify competing writers to current search results; keep cache and saved filters as separate stores.

stages.question: Can cancellation, cached responses and network pages race?
stages.reason: A single coordinator owns generation, cancellation and visible page identity.
stages.title: Merge the request-state writers

solutions.title: Server queries with revision-guarded results
tradeoffs: Network latency remains visible; cancellation may not stop server work.
Server cursors must bind the chosen consistency policy.
